reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that sports prediction markets exhibit systematic bias between observed prices and true win probabilities. This manifests in two ways: first, TTE-conditional calibration reveals that price accuracy varies with time-to-expiry, suggesting liquidity or information decay effects. Second, parlay contracts systematically overprice with increasing leg count, indicating multiplicative error propagation. These phenomena are modeled using parametric calibration functions (power-logit, Platt scaling, Prelec-II) which map raw prices to calibrated probabilities. The inflation ratio R = P_exec / ∏ p_j captures this mispricing directly. The regression β̂_1 ≈ 0.029 shows consistent per-leg inflation, implying a predictable drift in parlay pricing. These primitives form a dual framework: one for static calibration and another for dynamic consistency checks. Failure modes include insufficient data in sparse TTE bins or non-independent leg executions. The mathematical structure supports both Bayesian inference (via calibrated probabilities) and state-space modeling (via inflation tracking).
